passage:
Monday. Yusuf told three classmates that Abhinav had been sent to the principal for stealing a pen. It wasn't true; he had only wanted to be the one with news.

Tuesday. "Yusuf, please stay after the bell," the teacher said. His mouth went dry. He thought of saying, "Not me." Instead he said, "I said it, and it wasn't true. I'm sorry." The teacher told him he would miss the next games period and that his parents would be told.

Wednesday. Missing games hurt. But Yusuf handed Abhinav a note: "Sorry for what I said." Abhinav read it twice and said, "Okay." Yusuf's shoulders dropped. He was not hiding any more.

qa.q: What did Yusuf tell three classmates?
qa.a: That Abhinav had been sent to the principal for stealing a pen.

qa.q: What was Yusuf thinking when his mouth went dry, and what did he decide?
qa.a: He was scared and thought of saying "Not me," but decided to admit it and apologise.

qa.q: Why was telling the truth the better choice for Yusuf?
qa.a: The consequences hurt, like missing games and his parents being told, but lying would have hurt more and kept him hiding.

qa.q: How might Abhinav have felt reading the note?
qa.a: Abhinav read it twice, so it likely mattered, though Abhinav only said "Okay," which suggests Abhinav may still be sorting out his feelings.

grounding: A teacher hears about a rumour and calls the child, who honestly says what he did and apologises, accepting the consequences.

passage:
"Sangeeta, please stay after class."
Her stomach dropped. Joseph Sir waited until the room was empty.
"I've heard that you told people Rohan cheated on the maths quiz. Is that true?"
Sangeeta wanted to say no. She wanted to say someone else started it.
"Sangeeta?"
She took a breath. "Yes, Sir. I said it. I was angry because he got a better mark."
"Thank you for being honest. That was hard."
"Am I in trouble?"
"There'll be consequences. You'll apologise to Rohan and help me set the record straight with the class. But lying would have made it much worse."
Sangeeta nodded. "I'm sorry."

qa.q: What did Sangeeta tell people about Rohan?
qa.a: That he cheated on the maths quiz.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta feel when Joseph Sir asked her to stay?
qa.a: She felt scared, her stomach dropping.

qa.q: Why was Sangeeta's honest answer better than lying?
qa.a: It meant she could apologise and help fix it, while lying would have made things much worse.

qa.q: How might Joseph Sir see Sangeeta's honesty?
qa.a: Joseph Sir respects it, thanking her and saying it was hard to do.

grounding: A teacher calls a girl about a rumour; she is scared but admits it and apologises, accepting consequences instead of lying.

passage:
I'm Vikas. In Class 5, I told everyone that a boy called Ronit had been caught stealing from the canteen. I made it up because he laughed at my football.
The next day, Ayesha Ma'am called me to the staffroom. My hands were shaking.
She asked, "Did you start this story about Ronit?"
I wanted to lie so badly. I could blame someone else. But she was looking at me calmly, waiting.
"Yes, Ma'am. I made it up. I'm sorry."
She nodded. "Thank you for telling me the truth." I had to apologise to Ronit in front of the class and miss football practice for a week. It hurt. But I think lying would have hurt more.

qa.q: What did Vikas say Ronit had been caught doing?
How did Vikas feel when Ayesha Ma'am called him?
qa.a: Vikas felt scared, with shaking hands.
An apology to Ronit in front of the class and missing football practice for a week.

qa.q: How might Ayesha Ma'am have felt when Vikas told the truth?
qa.a: She seemed to appreciate the honesty, calmly thanking Vikas for it.

grounding: A teacher calls Vikas about a rumour Vikas made up; Vikas is scared but admits it, apologises and accepts consequences.
